sovereign_country.strategic_role: 亚太高客单价数字内容、游戏出海与本土电商合规

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Korea-United States Free Trade Agreement (KORUS FTA)
Korea-United Kingdom Double Taxation Avoidance Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 14119, effective March 24, 2021) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality (Act No. 14120); Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU); Commercial Act (Act No. 17905) for corporate governance and shareholder disclosure obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if issued in a member state) or Consular Legalization (if issued in a non-member state); for Korea, the document is domestic and requires no apostille if used domestically, but for foreign use, apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) is required.
Hague Apostille via MOFA for foreign use; Consular Legalization for non-member states; domestic use requires no authentication.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney (이사회 결의서 / 위임장)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Board of Directors (notarized by a Korean notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Korean notary, then Hague Apostille via MOFA for member states; Consular Legalization for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company founders (notarized by a Korean notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Korean notary, then Hague Apostille via MOFA for member states; Consular Legalization for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via MOFA for member states; Consular Legalization for non-member states; domestic use requires no authentication.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own sanctions list (Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, including foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any trigger event (e.g., change in ownership). All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years. For hyper-casual gaming entities, additional scrutiny is applied to payment rails (AdMob, AppLovin) to ensure no sanctioned entities are involved in ad networks or payment processors. The compliance officer must certify that no matches are found before incorporation proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Registry Online (I-REGIST) – https://www.i-regist.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) for registration; English transliteration is permitted for foreign use but must be phonetically consistent. The name must include a legal form suffix such as '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa) for LLC. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. A four-tier naming convention applies: (1) distinctive element, (2) business purpose descriptor, (3) legal form suffix, and (4) optional English transliteration. The name must not contain any prohibited tokens without prior ministerial approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 543 through 613 governing a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), including Articles 543, 545, 546, 548, 549, 551, 553, 557, 558, 560, 566, 568, 571, 584, 585, 592 and 613; the Registration of Commercial Matters Act (Act No. 6043, as amended); the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act; and, for non-resident shareholders, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 9697, as amended).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office, under the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, with preliminary name search conducted through the Supreme Court Internet Registration System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company under the Registration of Commercial Matters Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the contribution payment certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The Articles of Incorporation must specify the number of equity interests and the amount of each member's contribution, and each member must fully perform the contribution before incorporation registration. Cash contributions must be deposited in a bank subscription account in the company's name and evidenced by a contribution certificate; no escrow or blocked-account arrangement is mandated by Korean law. In-kind contributions must be appraised by a court-appointed expert. The Korean court registration fee is not flat: registration license tax is calculated ad valorem on declared capital at 0.4 percent, subject to a statutory minimum of KRW 22,500, plus 20 percent local education tax; therefore, no fixed USD state fee is reported in the fee field.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT ON [DATE]. 1. CONVENING AND QUORUM. The undersigned, being all the directors of Yuhan Hoesa named in the notarized Articles of Incorporation, hereby waive notice of meeting and act as the first board of directors of the company, constituting a full quorum. All resolutions below are adopted unanimously and are effective as of the date of this instrument. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that the initial members and equity interests of the company are subscribed as follows: [name of first member] subscribes for [number] equity interests for a contribution of [amount]; [name of second member] subscribes for [number] equity interests for a contribution of [amount]. The aggregate paid-up capital is [currency and amount], and each member shall pay his or her contribution in full into a designated bank subscription account before incorporation registration, all in accordance with Articles 548 and 551 of the Commercial Act. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company shall be located at [full address], Republic of Korea, and that the Chief Executive Officer is authorized to sign, execute, and deliver the lease agreement, utility agreements, and every instrument necessary to establish and register the office with the competent registry, tax office, and local authorities. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the company shall open deposit, payment, and treasury management accounts at [bank], and that the following individuals, namely [name and title], shall be authorized signatories, each acting singly or jointly as specified on the signature card, with full authority to open, operate, transfer funds, close, and sign all banking agreements and electronic banking mandates on behalf of the company. 5. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer/Dae-pyo Imsa of the company, with full authority to manage the ordinary business of the company and to represent the company before third parties, government agencies, courts, and tax authorities, and that [name] is appointed Auditor/Gam-sa to the extent required by the Commercial Act and the Articles. 6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Chief Executive Officer and the directors are jointly and severally authorized to prepare and file the incorporation registration, business registration, tax filings, corporate seal registration, game rating and classification applications, banking forms, and all related corporate governance records, and to retain legal counsel, accountants, and other advisors as may be necessary. This resolution is effective immediately, may be executed in counterparts, and remains in full force until amended or revoked by a valid resolution of the members or directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation, Foreign Investment Screening, and Corporate Structure Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration System of the Republic of Korea, administered by the Court Administration Office; Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest KOREA office for foreign-investor guidance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exact and confusingly similar name search against the Korean commercial registry using the Supreme Court Internet Registration System. Confirm that the proposed corporate name in English and Korean does not infringe any existing registered trade name and that the business purpose is lawful under Article 545 of the Commercial Act. For non-resident incorporators, verify the list of restricted sectors and prepare the Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification if the foreign investment report thresholds are met. Obtain certified passport pages and, where required, apostilled or legalized corporate documents. Identify the registered office address and confirm the territorial jurisdiction of the court registry and district tax office.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of all members and directors
Apostilled or legalized power of attorney, if any
Foreign investment notification form, if applicable
Name search result from the Internet Registration System
Draft registered-office lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search fails, select an alternative name and re-run the search. If foreign investment review is triggered, submit supplemental source-of-funds and business-model documents within the statutory cure period. If the online system issues a deficiency notice, respond through the portal before the deadline to avoid deemed withdrawal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Execution of Subscription Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public of the Republic of Korea assigned to the local district court in the jurisdiction of the company's registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft bilingual Korean and English Articles of Incorporation for a Yuhan Hoesa containing all mandatory matters under Article 545 of the Commercial Act: corporate purpose, trade name, registered office, names and contributions of members, aggregate capital, transferability restrictions on equity interests, and method of public notice. The incorporators must execute the Articles by signature or corporate seal. The Korean text will be controlling, so the operative Korean purpose clause must accurately cover ISIC 5820 software development and mobile game publishing. The notary will verify the legality of the purpose, attest the signatures, and issue a notarial certificate to be annexed to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Notarized original Articles of Incorporation
Subscription list and capital allocation schedule
Written consents of directors and auditor
Identity documents of all incorporators
Corporate seal specimen, if a seal is used
Legalization or apostille of foreign member documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect, amend the Articles, re-execute before the same or another notary, and obtain a fresh notarial certificate. If the purpose clause is considered too broad or unlawful, narrow the business purpose and resubmit the corrected Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Contributions and Issuance of Contribution Payment Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea at which the subscription account is opened, supervised by the Financial Supervisory Service; for in-kind contributions, a court-appointed appraiser.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary subscription deposit account in the name of the company being incorporated and have each member remit the full amount of his or her contribution before registration. For cash contributions, obtain a Korean bank deposit certificate or passbook confirmation specifying the depositor, bank, account number, and amount. For in-kind contributions, obtain a court-appointed appraisal report and annex it to the registration dossier. The account is not an escrow account and no statutory blocked-account authorization is required. The bank will require customer due diligence and source-of-funds declarations for each contributing member. The contribution certificate must remain in the company file because the court registry will inspect it before entering the incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Bank subscription account opening form
KYC and source-of-funds declarations
Member passport copies
Deposit certificate or bank confirmation
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Contribution schedule approved by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank defers account opening for enhanced due diligence, provide sworn source-of-funds letters and bank statements, or select another licensed bank. If the contribution has not been fully paid, complete the shortfall before registration, because a deficiency will cause the court registry to suspend the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Incorporation Registration with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the District Court for the district in which the registered office is located, for example the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registry, as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application for a limited liability company under the Registration of Commercial Matters Act within two weeks after the completion of capital contributions. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, contribution certificate, written consents of directors and auditor, identity proof of officers, and a power of attorney if filing is made by a representative. Pay the court registration license tax and local education surtax. The registry will conduct a legality review and, if satisfied, register the company in the commercial register and issue a certified corporate registration certificate. Legal personality of the Yuhan Hoesa is created only upon this registration; therefore, verify all attached documents for exactness before submission.
required_dossiers: Registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Contribution payment certificate
Director and auditor consent statements
Identity documents of directors and auditor
Power of attorney, if applicable
Payment receipt for court registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure the stated deficiency before the prescribed deadline. If the application is rejected, file an objection or immediate appeal under the Registration of Commercial Matters Act, or withdraw and re-file after correcting the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Tax Registrations, Bank Account Activation, and Corporate Governance Handover
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District tax office of the National Tax Service with jurisdiction over the registered office; local municipal government for local taxes; the designated commercial bank for account activation; and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or designated foreign exchange bank for any post-incorporation foreign investment report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days from the commencement of business, apply for a business registration certificate at the district tax office using the certified corporate registration certificate; register for value added tax and corporate income tax; and enrol as a withholding agent for employee income tax. Activate the temporary subscription account as a corporate operating account by presenting the certified registration and corporate seal certificate. Pass and retain final board resolutions formalizing the corporate governance structure, bank signatories, and registered office. If the Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification thresholds are met, file the post-incorporation foreign investment report. For hyper-casual mobile game publishing, submit the game content classification application to the Game Rating and Administration Committee before commercial distribution; this is a content-age rating requirement and a separate statutory obligation from any physical or industrial operating license.
required_dossiers: Certified corporate registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate
Business registration application form
Registered-office lease agreement and utility bill
Bank activation forms and authorized signatory list
Foreign investment report form, if applicable
Game Rating and Administration Committee classification application, if distributing in Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the registered office, provide a lease amendment and landlord identity certificate. If the bank declines account activation, complete enhanced due diligence with source-of-wealth letters. If the game rating application is returned, revise the game information pack and resubmit before launch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - pure digital software and mobile game publishing under ISIC 5820, with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operations. A Game Rating and Administration Committee content classification is a separate statutory content-age rating obligation, not an industrial operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no physical Environmental Impact Assessment is required for head-office based software and game publishing under ISIC 5820. Any future leased office fit-out, data center construction, or dedicated server facility would be assessed at that time under ordinary municipal building and environmental rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the business generates zero process wastewater, negligible volatile organic compound emissions, and no hazardous waste streams from manufacturing. If the company later owns and operates physical servers or data centers, the Ministry of Environment energy efficiency, electronic waste, and waste disposal rules would apply at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no factory, warehouse, chemical installation, or large physical facility requires a Civil Defense fire permit or structural load inspection. As a standard office employer, Yuhan Hoesa must still comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act by providing a safe workplace, fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, and basic workplace safety instruction, and the leased building must maintain its own fire safety certification under the Act on Fire Prevention and Safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic tax portal; customs declarations and export clearances are processed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the foreign investor must first file an initial foreign investment notification with KOTRA or through an authorized foreign exchange bank, then submit the standard Application for Business Registration to the competent district tax office serving the entity's registered address. The application must include the articles of incorporation, a copy of the director's identification, a lease agreement or title evidence for the domestic business address, and a statement of business purpose. Once verified, NTS issues the 10-digit business registration number and the Business Registration Certificate, which serves as the entity's Korean Tax Identification Number for corporate income tax and VAT. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a Korean permanent establishment, a domestic tax representative must be appointed to complete the registration, retain VAT records, issue electronic tax invoices, and communicate with NTS through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not operate a check-the-box election for ordinary limited liability companies. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is automatically taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and there are no hybrid mismatch elections for this standard commercial entity. Certain specially regulated investment vehicles have separate optional tax regimes, but they are inapplicable to a hyper-casual game publishing company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None. All businesses, including foreign-invested domestic companies, must register for VAT from the commencement of business irrespective of revenue volume. A business that expects annual taxable supplies below the statutory simplified taxpayer ceiling may be treated as a simplified taxpayer, but registration itself is still mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Tax invoices must be issued electronically through an NTS-certified e-tax invoice system and transmitted to NTS through HomeTax. Electronic invoices must be reported to NTS no later than the day following the issuance date. Korea does not operate a real-time transaction-level fiscal clearance or digital stamping system; the mandate is a near-real-time electronic tax invoice reporting regime. For exports, an electronic export declaration is also filed with Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, and the data is made available to NTS under an integrated information-sharing mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to the export of tangible goods where the goods are actually shipped outside Korea and an export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service. For services, zero-rating is available for specifically enumerated service categories, including international transportation and services physically or legally consumed entirely outside Korea; in the hyper-casual mobile game context, advertising and service revenues derived from overseas publishers may qualify as zero-rated exported services when the recipient is a non-resident business, the services are used outside Korea, and payment is collected through a foreign exchange license or approved domestic settlement method. The exporter must retain documentary evidence of the export transaction, the tax invoice, and proof of foreign currency repatriation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic Export Declaration and export clearance certificate
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing actual departure from Korea
Commercial Invoice and Packing List describing the exported goods or service scope
Foreign Exchange Repatriation Confirmation issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing inward remittance of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service maintain digital integration of export declarations, e-tax invoices, foreign exchange settlement records, and corporate VAT returns. If the exporter cannot substantiate zero-rating through the required documentation bundle, NTS will deny the 0% rate and assess VAT at 10% on the gross export amount, with statutory additional taxes and interest calculated from the date the refund was paid or the zero-rating was claimed. Deliberate submission of false export declarations, fabricated foreign exchange settlement certificates, or overdeclared export values exposes the company to criminal tax investigation, customs record falsification penalties, revocation of export benefits, and clawback of all refunds received together with penalties up to the amount of tax evaded.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central execution authority, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting as the supreme foreign exchange administrative agency under the framework of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized managed-float currency regime. The Korean won (KRW) is materially convertible for both current account items, such as advertising, royalty, and software licensing payments, and capital account items, including foreign direct investment equity subscription and shareholder loans, subject to the declaration, reporting, or license duties imposed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. There is no mandatory surrender of export or service proceeds to the central bank; instead, foreign currency receipts may be held in domestic foreign-currency deposit accounts at authorized foreign exchange banks. Profit remittance is permitted once solvency, audit, and corporate income tax obligations are demonstrated, but the offshore parent must provide board minutes, audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and the underlying economic substance documentation for ad-network revenue to prove the outflow is a genuine distribution or service payment. Capital account transactions, including cross-border loans, acquisitions, and equity injections, are separately reportable to MOEF/BOK through the reporting bank. The practical constraint is not absolute convertibility but documentary completeness, strict foreign exchange purpose coding, and the statutory requirement that every material transaction be routed through a domestically licensed foreign exchange bank. Entities using foreign unlicensed EMI accounts for settlement or unnecessarily converting KRW offshore may encounter anti-money laundering scrutiny, delayed repatriation, and potential administrative penalties. Therefore, treasury design should treat KRW as freely usable inside South Korea but operationally dependent on a licensed domestic bank for seamless regulatory reporting and compliance clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory conversion or surrender requirement for export/service proceeds under the Korean framework. A resident exporter must collect foreign currency revenues through an authorized foreign exchange bank and must, as a general rule, complete collection within five years from the date of export declaration for physical goods; for digital gaming services and ad-network proceeds, the collection window is managed under the same foreign exchange bank supervision, with extension available upon justifiable documentary request. The foreign currency may remain held in a foreign-currency deposit account at a domestic Tier-1 bank, and converted to KRW when operational liquidity requires. Conversion must be reported under the approved foreign exchange purpose code, and any divergence between the invoiced contract, the settlement instruction, and the underlying ad-network payout log may trigger a customs or BOK examination.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Operational Account and KRW Business Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Licensed only as an auxiliary tool for international executives' discretionary expenses, an offshore digital EMI is legally impracticable as the primary clearing rail for this Korean entity. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, any inbound capital injection must be notified through a designated domestic foreign exchange bank, and the company's capital verification certificate must be issued by a Korean account bank. Foreign EMIs without a Korean banking license cannot register the FDI notification, cannot issue valid domestic securities subscription receipts for capital verification, and are not admissible as a licensed foreign exchange bank for tax filings or trade settlement. South Korean supervisory practice effectively requires statutory account operation to reside onshore with a Tier-1 bank; using an EMI for core treasury would create regulatory discomfort, purpose-code failures, and AML red flags on aggregated ad-marketplace payouts. Thus, the blueprint should use domestic Tier-1 banks for both escrow and operational rails, with EMI accounts optional only for non-operational administrative expenses and never for proceeds collection or equity injection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required as a clear default rule. Korean banks conduct corporate onboarding through an in-branch interview of the statutory representative director or a formally authorized director with board-approved signing authority. For a non-resident director not physically present in Korea, remote contactless onboarding is generally not available at the top-tier banks for newly formed companies involving foreign shareholders. A compliant substitute is an in-person identity verification before an overseas branch of the same Korean bank, a Korean consular official, or a notary public recognized under the Apostille Convention, followed by couriered original signatures and a sealed certificate of authorized signatories. The bank will require the corporate seal certificate, certificate of incorporation, shareholder register, ultimate beneficial owner declarations, and board resolution confirming account signatories. These documents must be apostilled or consular-legalized and translated into Korean before the compliance committee will approve the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ad-network revenue settlements from multiple foreign parties (AdMob, AppLovin) are aggregated and commingled with user micro-transactions, making the underlying counterparty architecture opaque and difficult to align with passive income declarations or royalty licensing agreements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury packet consisting of: official accounting currency statements from each ad-network portal, monthly payout reconciliation ledgers, contract addenda with Google LLC and AppLovin Corporation, detail of traffic supply partners, registered user geographic concentration reports, data-processing and ad-serving agreements, and a signed internal control memorandum proving that no third-party payment processing shell or unlicensed payment gateway stands between the entity and the ad-network payors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners injecting capital through family or nominee-linked wiring channels, creating ambiguity over the genuine source of funds and the economic substance of the Korean operating entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A source-of-wealth and source-of-funds file for every UBO and shareholder holding 10% or more: certified bank statements for the previous six months, audited financial statements of the foreign parent, personal tax returns or corporate filings, share transfer documentation, apostilled incorporation documents of each intermediate holding company, a fund-flow chart explaining every circulating deposit between the parent group and the Korean entity, and a personal equity injection declaration signed under penalty of false-statement liability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The hyper-casual mobile game business may generate export revenue to low-risk tax havens or high-risk traffic markets, causing jurisdiction-based sanctions screening and adverse-media failures under the bank's transaction monitoring program.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A geographical revenue waterfall report by country, sanctions and embargo screening results for all app publishing counterparts, a media and regulatory search file for the owning group, traffic quality reports from major ad networks, certificates of tax residence for each material counterparty, and a signed letter from the compliance officer demonstrating that storefront operations and digital advertising do not involve transactions with OFAC, EU, or UN-sanctioned parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Optimization of royalty and service payments to a foreign head office may be repriced as intra-group margin stripping, triggering regulatory suspicion of transfer-pricing manipulation and disguised dividend repatriation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A validated transfer-pricing study compliant with OECD BEPS guidelines, the IP licensing and trademark agreement, an economic substance report showing where the gaming development, game operations, traffic acquisition, and risk management functions are performed, detailed intellectual property registration records, invoices for intercompany services with time-and-cost substantiation, and the Korean entity's tax declaration demonstrating arm's-length pricing for all royalties, management fees, and advertising cost contributions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent investor must file the Foreign Investment Notification through a domestic designated foreign exchange bank before the equity wire is released. The remitting bank will transmit a SWIFT MT103 with the investor's exact corporate name and a strict purpose code corresponding to equity investment in a Korean resident enterprise; the receiving Korean bank credits the capital escrow account under the name of the Korean entity and issues the Certificate of Import of Capital Goods where applicable. After the equity funds are credited, the bank verifies the amount against the FDI declaration, obtains a Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation, and issues the capital verification certificate required by the Commercial Act. Prior to distribution to the operational account, the bank requires the final UBO structure, the board resolution approving the share subscription, and the executed articles of incorporation. For any shareholder loan component, the offshore lender must also file a loan agreement and purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and the debt facility must be distinguished from equity in internal treasury records to avoid accidental dividend withholding characterizations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement for non-digital goods and services involving Korean suppliers should use SWIFT MT103 for immediate operative balance transfers, with reference to the correct outbound foreign exchange purpose code and the supporting contract, invoice, and customs report. For trade involving disruptive logistics, Korean trade partners, or higher-ticket transactions, the preferred rail is an Irrevocable Confirmed Commercial Letter of Credit substantiated by a sales contract, packing list, commercial invoice, and clean transport document. Documentary Collections may be used only where the counterparty has a proven settlement history and the bank's compliance committee accepts the trade documentation. For recurring international payments to the ad networks and global app stores, the treasury team should execute automated SWIFT payment instructions from the domestic KRW account to the parent or overseas service provider's account, each instruction backed by a vendor invoice, monthly settlement statement, ad-network payout report, and withholding tax computation where Korea domestic withholding rules apply. All outbound transactions must pass through the designated FX bank's real-time sanctions, UBO, and adverse-media filters before the MT103 is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Korean won forward contracts onshore, executed with a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank, limited to underlying current-account exposure arising from ad-network settlements, licensing revenues, and contracted operating costs

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted offshore for KRW exposure, permissible only as a hedge for non-resident counterparties with genuine and documented Korean won exposure, not as a speculative leverage vehicle

Currency swaps between KRW and USD for matching long-term shareholder-loan or FDI-related cash-flow exposures, conditional on the existence of a real receivables or payables stream and approved foreign exchange purpose coding

Plain-vanilla FX options embedded in treasury hedging programs for protection against adverse KRW movements, requiring board approval and an underlying current or capital account transaction to satisfy the banks' compliance and suitability standards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local income tax surcharge return, accompanied by statutory financial statements and tax reconciliation schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and the competent municipal/provincial local government tax authority in which the registered office is located.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, due no later than 31 March of the following calendar year. E-filed returns enjoy an automatic one-month filing extension to 30 April, and a further NTS-approved extension to 31 July is available for taxpayers with international transactions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the tax properly due if the return is not filed by the deadline; 10% additional tax for under-reporting taxable income; 0.022% per-day overdue interest on unpaid tax; repeated delinquency allows the NTS to seize bank accounts and trade receivables, cancel the business registration, and refer the representative for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual VAT returns, electronic tax invoices, and VAT payment for hyper-casual game advertising revenue and cross-border ad-network costs (AdMob/AppLovin).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system and the Korea Approved Tax Invoice system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First VAT period (1 January to 30 June): filed by 25 July of the same year. Second VAT period (1 July to 31 December): filed by 25 January of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported VAT attracts an additional tax of 10% of the unpaid VAT; fraudulent or aggravated non-reporting attracts 20%; overdue interest accrues at 0.022% per day; persistent failure triggers VAT registration cancellation, asset attachment, and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual year-end withholding settlement of employee wage and global income taxes, including employer payment certificates for wages, bonuses, severance, and stock-based compensation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding and payment of wage income tax by the 10th day of the following month; annual wage-payment certificate (annual settlement reconciliation) must be filed by 10 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold: 10% additional tax on the unwithheld amount; late remittance: 0.022% daily late-interest tax; failure to submit each wage-payment certificate: KRW 5,000 per certificate, with block-listing on NTS non-filer systems.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual international transaction statement and foreign payee payment certificates covering cross-border software, advertising, royalty and digital marketing service payments to AdMob, AppLovin and other foreign vendors.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) International Taxation Division and, where the transaction exceeds the reporting threshold, the competent foreign-exchange bank and the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual international transaction statement accompanies the corporate income tax filing by 31 March for a 31 December year-end; payment certificates for income paid to nonresident corporations are due by the 10th day of the month following each payment, with final annual reconciliation at the CIT due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or misstatement of international transactions exposes the company to administrative fines of up to KRW 20,000,000 under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (approximately USD 15,000), loss of tax deduction for foreign advertising costs, and criminal liability for intentional false reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register and commercial-registry consistency review, certifying the register of members, register of directors, register of charges, minute book, and registered-office records, and filing any required registry amendments.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the competent Korean District Court for actual amendments; the annual consistency review itself is prepared for the management and tax files and kept in the statutory records rather than publicly filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual register audit must be completed before the 31 March corporate tax filing deadline; any registration event (change of directors or auditors, transfer of shares, change of registered office, capital change) must be filed with the court registry within two weeks of the event; beneficial-ownership banking files must be refreshed within 30 days of any shareholding transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a required registry amendment within the two-week period creates an administrative fine under the Commercial Act of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800); uncurrent registers can invalidate certain corporate acts, delay financing, and expose directors to fiduciary mismanagement claims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members' resolution approving the statutory financial statements, profit appropriation or loss absorption, and confirmation of distributions in accordance with Korean Commercial Act restrictions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book and corporate secretarial records; a copy is attached to the annual CIT return when filed with the National Tax Service.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each fiscal year-end, i.e., no later than 31 March for a 31 December year-end; a sole-member or unanimous-member Yuhan Hoesa may approve by written consent without a formal physical meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate government fine applies solely for late internal approval, but directors who approve dividends while the company fails statutory capital tests are jointly and severally liable under the Commercial Act; failure to include approved statements in the CIT return triggers the CIT non-filing and underreporting penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified independent auditor's report and audited financial statements, prepared when the Yuhan Hoesa meets the mandatory external audit thresholds.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) as an attachment to the corporate income tax return, and a copy delivered to the shareholders/members and board of directors and retained in the statutory books.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent audit must be completed before the ordinary members' meeting and the CIT filing, therefore ordinarily before 31 March following the fiscal year-end; auditor appointment should occur early enough to permit at least six weeks of audit fieldwork before that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the mandatory threshold is crossed, failure to appoint an outside auditor or to submit audited statements violates the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; penalties include fines of up to KRW 100,000,000 for the company and responsible officers, automatic rejection of the tax return as incomplete, and referral for suspension or cancellation of business privileges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (as amended by the current enforcement decree), a Yuhan Hoesa is required to appoint a certified public accountant as external auditor if any one of the following thresholds is met: (i) balance-sheet total assets at the preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); (ii) annual turnover/revenue equals or exceeds KRW 20,000,000,000 (approximately USD 15,000,000); or (iii) the average number of full-time employees during the preceding year equals or exceeds 150. A statutory audit is also mandatory for any Korean entity that is listed on KOSPI/KOSDAQ, engages in licensed financial services, or has publicly offered bonds. Companies below these ceilings have no automatic statutory audit obligation solely because of LLC status, but shareholders, creditors with legal standing, or the National Tax Service may validly request a special audit under the Commercial Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (KIFRS) for mandatory-audit companies; for a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa, Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), including the SME simplified accounting standards, may be elected, but financial statements must present a true and fair view and reconcile to KIFRS-compliant figures when an external audit is required. The statutory filing to the NTS must be in Korean won; if the functional currency is USD, a KRW translation schedule is mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and the Commercial Act, the Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an up-to-date beneficial ownership register at its registered office. Every shareholding transfer or change in control must be recorded in the Register of Members and submitted to the Commercial Registry within 14 days; the bank AML/KYC file must be updated within 30 days. Annually, before the corporate tax return is filed, the corporate secretary must circulate to all members a confirmation of the register of members and beneficial owner schedule, obtain a signed confirmation or documented non-response, and preserve it in the minute book. No separate annual government UBO return is imposed on private Yuhan Hoesas, but if the confirmation reveals a mismatch with registered ownership, the company must report a suspicious transaction to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the FTRA.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per annum for a registered address, corporate secretarial support, and statutory-register custody in Seoul or a major Korean metropolitan jurisdiction.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 - USD 20,000 per annum for a standard Yuhan Hoesa audit under Korean IFRS/K-GAAP, depending on transaction volume and international payment complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% maximum national corporate income tax rate for taxable income above KRW 300 billion; with the 10% local income tax surtax, the top combined statutory rate is 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive national rates apply: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion. Korea provides R&D tax credits of approximately 25%-50% of qualifying R&D and software development expenditure, preferential tax holidays for certain foreign-invested high-technology zones, and SME tax reductions. No general patent-box or effective zero-rate free-zone regime is available for hyper-casual mobile game publishing income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Amount Computation Return and attached schedules, filed electronically through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations with fiscal years longer than six months must also make semi-annual preliminary corporate income tax payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the immediately following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Total Sales and Gross Business Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from hyper-casual mobile game publishing, including AdMob and AppLovin advertising payouts, in-app purchases, and ancillary digital content sales, before intercompany adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income if the Korean entity is a tax resident. If the actual revenue is earned through a foreign subsidiary or platform account, Korean-sourcing and permanent establishment rules may require income to be reattributed to the Korean taxpayer. Do not net advertising platform fees unless the contractual arrangement is legal and evidenced by third-party statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Non-Deductible Expenses and Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses disallowed or limited for corporate income tax purposes, including excessive entertainment costs, non-statutory reserves, unlawful foreign payments, and excessive intercompany management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties, interest, and technical service fees paid to non-resident related parties are deductible only if the payment is at arm's length, reflected in the economic substance of the transaction, and accompanied by proper withholding tax remittance. A payment made without satisfying beneficial ownership and residence documentation will be denied and recharacterized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income derived from net accounting profit after statutory add-backs and deductions, forming the base for progressive corporate income tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim deductions for expenses attributable to unremitted foreign payouts if the corresponding withholding tax has not been paid. Unrealized foreign exchange losses, undeclared constructive dividends, and artificial cost allocations to non-resident affiliates must be reversed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Foreign Tax Credit and Domestic Withholding Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits claimed for foreign income taxes paid on Korean-resident income that is also taxable in Korea, and for domestic withholding taxes previously deducted at source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim a foreign tax credit, attach the foreign tax return or assessment notice and translate the underlying income. The credit is limited to the Korean corporate income tax attributable to foreign-source income. Non-resident shareholders cannot use this line for Korean withholding tax suffered on outbound dividends or royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Transfer Pricing Adjustment and Constructive Dividend or Deemed Donation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Voluntary or assessed arm's-length adjustments computed under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, including corrections to ad monetization fees, IP royalties, and intercompany debt interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean gaming entity underpriced ad-monetization services to its overseas parent or overpaid royalties to a low-tax affiliate, the excess amount is taxable as an expense adjustment and may be reclassified as a constructive dividend or deemed donation to the non-resident shareholder. Withholding tax, interest, and penalty surtax are applied from the original payment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Withholding Tax on Outbound Dividends, Royalties, and Interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of profit repatriation subject to statutory withholding tax and the 10% local income tax surtax on payments to non-resident shareholders and foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify every non-resident recipient by tax residence and beneficial ownership before filing. Unless a valid Tax Residency Certificate and treaty relief application are on file, withhold and remit 22% on gross dividends, royalties, and interest. Failure to withhold makes the Korean entity and its responsible directors jointly liable for the uncollected amount plus penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a valid extension triggers an unfiled-return additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax. An incorrect underreported return attracts a 10% negligence surtax, increased to 40% for fraudulent or concealment-based evasion. Unpaid corporate income tax accrues daily delinquency surcharges from the statutory due date until fully settled. Willful non-filing or false filing can also trigger criminal tax evasion proceedings against the taxpayer and responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on gross dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders, composed of 20% national dividend withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax, unless an applicable bilateral income tax treaty reduces the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief before payment, the non-resident recipient must deliver a Tax Residency Certificate issued by its home tax authority within the prior six months, a statement of beneficial ownership confirming that the recipient has the right to use and enjoy the income, and the NTS-approved application for tax exemption or reduction by a non-resident under a tax treaty. The Korean withholding agent must review and retain these documents before applying the reduced rate. If documentation is incomplete or the recipient is a conduit or pass-through entity, withholding at the full 22% statutory rate is mandatory. Excess withheld tax may be reclaimed by the non-resident through the NTS refund procedure within the statutory claim period, generally three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid to non-residents are both subject to a 22% domestic statutory gross withholding tax composed of 20% national tax plus 2% local surtax. Under Korean double tax treaties, royalty rates are commonly reduced to 10%-15% and interest rates to 10%-15%, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and the arrangement has economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is required when cross-border related-party transactions with a single foreign related party exceed KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year; Master File preparation is required when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion; Country-by-Country reporting is required where the multinational group has consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulation for ordinary gaming companies, but the statutory substance-over-form doctrine, general anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership tests, and judicial corporate veil-piercing doctrine are applied strictly. A Korean hyper-casual game publisher must demonstrate core income-generating activity in Korea through local staff, offices, books, bank accounts, and management decisions. A shell entity that merely receives AdMob or AppLovin proceeds and remits profits offshore will be recharacterized, denied treaty benefits, or disregarded for Korean tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Offshore Digital Game Revenue Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using foreign bank accounts or third-party digital wallets to receive AdMob or AppLovin revenue without recording the receipts in the Korean entity's books; understating Korean user ad-monetization income; fabricating intercompany advertising service contracts to divert profits to a zero-tax or treaty-reduced jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, applied with the Framework Act on Taxes, authorizes criminal penalties of imprisonment and fines equal to several times the evaded tax, plus NTS additional tax of 40% on fraudulent underreporting. The underpaid tax is assessed retroactively with interest and daily delinquency surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director or officer is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, additional tax, and collection costs. NTS may attach personal bank accounts, blacklist the director on the serious delinquent taxpayer registry, impose an overseas travel ban, and the director may be criminally sentenced to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Non-Resident Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident shareholder or royalties and interest to a foreign affiliate without withholding and remitting the 22% statutory tax; applying a reduced treaty rate using an invalid Tax Residency Certificate or a nominee holder; disguising profit distributions as service fees or cost reimbursements to avoid withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is liable for the unwithheld tax plus an additional tax of up to 50% of the unremitted amount under the Framework Act on Taxes and the Corporate Income Tax Act. The underlying payment is disallowed as a deduction and the missing tax remains collectible from the Korean payer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign or direct the unlawful remittance are personally liable for the tax shortfall. NTS asset attachment, travel bans, blacklisting, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment of the responsible director or financial officer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse, Shell Company and AML Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a Hong Kong or Singapore shell company with no employees, office, or core income-generating activity as the licensed owner of Korean game IP solely to obtain a reduced DTA rate on royalty or dividend outflows; routing Korean consumer payments through foreign payment processors to obscure ultimate beneficial ownership and avoid Korean source taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korea applies its domestic general anti-abuse rule and the OECD-inspired principal purpose test to deny treaty benefits. The income is recharacterized as Korean-source taxable income of the ultimate beneficial owner, subject to 22% withholding or corporate income tax as applicable, plus a 40% fraud surtax and foreign exchange violation penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the judicial corporate veil-piercing doctrine and the Korean Commercial Act, directors who created or maintained the sham structure may be personally liable for the withheld tax and penalties. Their personal assets can be seized, they may be blacklisted and banned from overseas travel, and repeated or aggravated conduct may lead to criminal imprisonment.
